steps.concept: What a quadratic equation is and what 'solving' means
rubric: solving means finding the x values that make the equation true
a quadratic can have two solutions
steps.miniExample: In x² = 16, both x = 4 and x = −4 make it true.
steps.label: What “solving” means

steps.concept: Zero-product rule: if A × B = 0 then A = 0 or B = 0
rubric: if a product equals zero, at least one factor is zero
this only works when the other side is exactly zero
steps.label: Zero-product rule

steps.concept: Factoring x² + bx + c into (x + p)(x + q)
rubric: find two numbers p and q that multiply to c
the same two numbers add up to b
write the expression as (x + p)(x + q)
steps.miniExample: x² + 3x + 2: numbers 1 and 2 multiply to 2 and add to 3, so (x + 1)(x + 2).
steps.label: Factoring

steps.concept: Putting it together and checking the answer
rubric: factor, then apply the zero-product rule to get the solutions
check each solution by putting it back into the original equation
steps.label: Solve and check
